images.caption: "Der Sozialismus Siegt" (socialism is victorious) is one of the slogans that the East German regime used.  The tour bus left East Berlin, and the sun came out.  The last stop was a place where you could climb up steps and look over the wall into East Berlin.  This looks toward Potsdamer Platz, which had been one of busiest places in Berlin in the 1920s and 1930s.  In 1963, with the Wall, nothing but empty spaces and tank traps.  I took a photo over the barbed wine, then tried a shot through the barbed wire.  This is the result.  It is my favorite Berlin Wall photo.

images.caption: View from Berliner Dom (Berlin Cathedral) in the direction of Potsdamer Platz (Potsdam Square). In the foreground the boulevard Unter den Linden (Under the Linden Trees) with the Guard House, the Prince's Palace and the Bebelplatz are recognizable. The towers on the left of the picture are part of the Gendarmenmarket. In the background the skylines of Leipziger Platz and Potsdamer Platz are visible.
images.alt: View from Berliner Dom (Berlin Cathedral) in the direction of Potsdamer Platz (Potsdam Square).
